figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. Identification of C-glycosyltransferase AuCGT involved in the biosynthesis of stromemycin. (A) Gene cluster coding for stromemycin
biosynthesis. MT: methyltransferase, TF: transcription factor, and LP: lipase. (B) HPLC analysis of the extracts of A. ustus and its mutants. (C)
HPLC analysis of the extracts of A. nidulans strains. (D) In vitro assays of StmC with 2 and UDP-glucose by HPLC analysis. (E, F) Negative MS
spectra of products 1 and 2, respectively. (G) Biosynthetic pathway of stromemycin in A. ustus.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Targeted discovery of fungal glycosides by AuCGT-guided genome mining and MS-based metabolome analysis. (A) Phylogenetic
analysis of AuCGT and homologues with characterized fungal OGTs and bacterial CGTs. The asterisk indicates that the catalytic functions of GTs
were verified. (B) Clusters containing AuCGT and homologues from diverse fungi analyzed by antiSMASH 5.0 and MIBIG hits. Genes encoding
AuCGT homologues are shown in red, and genes encoding NR-PKS and HR-PKS are shown in blue and brownish red, respectively. The identities
(%) of these homologues to StmABC are shown above the cluster, respectively. (C) MS analysis of the characteristic fragment ions of
representative glycosides. (D) Characteristic fragment ions of representative glycoside candidates from strains Talaromyces spp. (E) Characteristic
fragment ions of representative glycoside candidates from strains Phaeomoniella chlamydospora, and Chalara longipes. (F) Characteristic fragment
ions of representative glycoside candidates from Verticillium dahliae and Fusarium sp.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. Chemical structures of new glycosides from three selected fungi. (A) Depside C-glycosides 3−12 isolated from T. cellulolyticus. (B)
Depside O-glycosides 16−23 isolated from P. chlamydospora. (C) α-Pyrone C-glycosides 26 and 27 isolated from V. dahliae. The glucosyl groups
are indicated in red, and the galactosyl groups are indicated in blue. Details of the structural determination of these new compounds are described
in the Supporting Information.

Figure 4. Combinatorial biosynthesis of unnatural glycosides in A. nidulans. (A) HPLC analysis of extracts engineered by A. nidulans. (B) Negative
MS spectra of products 30 and 31, positive MS spectrum of 32. (C) Chemical structures of products 30−32.
